messages:
maria: quick one — debugging a routing surprise. requests hitting `svc-internal` instead of `accounts-frontend` for `GET /v1/accounts/123/profile`. looks like a matcher tie. can we add a match-score breakdown in the console so you can see why one rule won?

kevin: +1 for breakdown. current heuristic is simple: exact host > host wildcard > path exact > path prefix > regex > header anchors (last). weights are pretty ad-hoc though.

sara: do we have an example where header anchor should outrank a host wildcard? iirc header anchors were intentionally low to avoid surprise overrides, but some customers expect auth-header routes to win.

maria: here's the minimal config that reproduced it: 
```yaml
- route: accounts-frontend
  host: accounts.example.com
  path_prefix: /v1/accounts

- route: svc-internal
  host: "*.example.com"
  header: {name: x-service, value: internal}
  path_prefix: /v1
```
request: Host: accounts.example.com, path: /v1/accounts/123/profile, header x-service: internal

kevin: interesting. wildcard host with header anchor + shorter path_prefix beats the exact host because of current tie-break math: we score host specificity (exact=100, wildcard=50), path length (per segment 10), header anchors +20. aggregate put svc-internal slightly higher.

ryan: that's the problem — absolute numbers feel brittle. We should normalize by # of segments and make header anchors proportional to how many anchors matched. e.g. score = host_score + (path_specificity / max_segments) * PATH_SCALE + header_score. then everyone understands why numbers change.

sara: agree on normalization. also for UX: show the per-rule contributions in the console and a human-readable explanation, not just raw numbers. e.g. "host exact +100; path segments (3/5) +60; header anchors matched +20 -> total 180"

maria: +1. Can we also surface the exact matching clause that applied (prefix vs exact vs capture) and show a small snippet of the route yaml in the trace? That would make debugging much faster.

kevin: prototype idea: add `match-explain` endpoint to gateway admin that returns breakdown and matched clauses. CLI: `gatewayctl match-explain --host accounts.example.com --path /v1/accounts/123/profile --header x-service=internal` -> returns JSON with score slices and matched clause ids.

maria: that would be perfect. For console UX, propose a lightweight bar + numbers next to each candidate route and a "Why this route" modal with the detailed breakdown and link to the rule in the config editor.

devex: also update docs and add a short note in the API reference about the new normalized scoring so existing customers don't get surprised. maybe add a changelog entry when we flip the normalization.

ryan: edge-case: regex routes that match deep captures can overshadow many segments — we should cap regex contribution to avoid regex=king. suggestion: regex_contrib = min( regex_raw_score, REGEX_CAP ) so it can't always dominate.

kevin: agreed. i'll open a draft RFC with: scoring formula, normalization approach, tie-breaker order, and a minimal `gatewayctl` proto for match-explain. can we get design for the modal?

maria: putting a small mock below for the modal layout (simple ascii):
```
[Route candidates]
1) accounts-frontend  ▇▇▇▇ 180  (reason: host exact + path exact)
   matched clauses: host:accounts.example.com, path_prefix:/v1/accounts
   link: open-config
2) svc-internal     ▇▇ 175  (reason: host wildcard + header anchor)
   matched clauses: host:*.example.com, header:x-service=internal, path_prefix:/v1
   link: open-config

[Why this route won]
- host exact +100
- path specificity +60
- header anchors +20
- normalization factor 0.95
-> final 180
```

kevin: nice. sara / ryan, want to sketch the modal microcopy? can we keep it short and avoid heavy math in default view — only show numbers if user clicks "advanced".

sara: yes. default: short sentence "accounts-frontend matched because host exact and longer path" + small bar. advanced: raw score table and matched clause ids.

devex: i'll write a short doc blurb and add a GIF showing "open modal -> see breakdown" for the release notes.

maria: thanks team — kevin, can you link the RFC in this thread when opened? if possible include a sample output for `gatewayctl match-explain` too. i'll try to repro with the normalization branch once it's up. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: canary deploy for gateway/routing-rules v0.17.3 started (deployment id: deploy-8672).

kevin: RFC opened: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/214-match-scoring (draft). added sample CLI output and a proposed UI wireframe. will follow up with a PR for gatewayctl.

maria: awesome — will test after canary. thanks!
